blockMcqs.question: What does a shortest-path algorithm minimize?
options: The number of edges on the path
The sum of edge weights along the path
The total edges needed to connect all nodes
The maximum single edge weight
blockMcqs.explanation: Edge counts and connection cost are different goals; shortest path adds up weights.

blockMcqs.question: In Dijkstra, when is a node's distance final?
options: When it is first discovered as a neighbor
After every edge has been relaxed once
The first time it is popped from the heap
Once the heap becomes empty
blockMcqs.explanation: Discovery only sets a tentative value; popping locks it in under the greedy rule.

blockMcqs.question: Why does Dijkstra's code skip entries where `d > dist[u]`?
options: Those nodes have negative edges
They are stale, superseded by a shorter distance
The heap is full and must be trimmed
It marks the node as unreachable
blockMcqs.explanation: Improving a distance leaves the old pair in the heap; the guard ignores it.

blockMcqs.question: How does Bellman-Ford detect a negative cycle?
options: A distance becomes exactly zero
The heap never empties
An edge still relaxes after V−1 passes
Two nodes share the same distance
blockMcqs.explanation: After V−1 passes all paths are settled, so a further improvement means a negative loop.

blockMcqs.question: Why must `k` be the outermost loop in Floyd-Warshall?
options: To keep the matrix symmetric
So distances are correct using intermediates 0..k first
To avoid integer overflow
Because i and j must be sorted
blockMcqs.explanation: Each pair must settle for intermediates up to k before k+1 is allowed.

blockMcqs.question: What gives union-find its near-constant per-op time?
options: Sorting the parent array each time
Union by rank plus path compression
A min-heap of group sizes
Storing groups in a hash map
blockMcqs.explanation: Shallow trees plus flattening on lookup yield the inverse-Ackermann bound.

blockMcqs.question: In Kruskal, why is an edge skipped?
options: Its weight exceeds the average
Its endpoints are already in the same group
It points to the source node
The heap is empty
blockMcqs.explanation: Union returns false when both ends share a root, since adding it forms a cycle.

blockMcqs.question: Which algorithm handles negative edge weights?
options: Dijkstra
Prim
Bellman-Ford
Kruskal
blockMcqs.explanation: Dijkstra's lock-in breaks on negatives; Prim and Kruskal solve MST, not paths.

blockMcqs.question: How does a shortest-path tree differ from an MST?
options: They are always the same set of edges
An MST minimizes distance from one source
It minimizes distance from a source, not total wiring
A shortest-path tree always has fewer edges
blockMcqs.explanation: The MST minimizes total edge weight to connect everyone, a different objective.

blockMcqs.question: Why can Google Maps rely on a Dijkstra-family algorithm?
options: Road graphs are always tiny
Travel times are never negative
All roads have equal weight
It needs all-pairs distances
blockMcqs.explanation: Non-negative weights are exactly what the greedy lock-in requires to stay correct.

blockMcqs.question: Why can't you fix negative edges by adding a constant to all weights?
options: It overflows the distance array
It penalizes longer paths more, changing the winner
Negative weights can't be shifted
It breaks the heap ordering
blockMcqs.explanation: More edges absorb more of the added constant, so the cheapest path can flip.
